| [CASE-313](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-313.md) | Removing the core of Ito and Kaneko's coupled-map network: in 12 of 12 seeds the periphery refills it to its former size and one-way structure within a million steps; half a core removed is made up from the periphery; a core made rare in influence is recovered by its own members | [LEAD-065](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-065.md) asked whether [QUESTION-132](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-132.md)'s candidate case, Ito and Kaneko's network of identical logistic maps with normalized, similarity-reinforced weights ([LIT-1842](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1842.md), [NOTE-1414](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1414.md)), refills its core when core units are removed. The model was reimplemented at the paper's parameters (N = 100, a = 3.97, c = 0.12, δ = 0.1) and grown for 3 × 10⁶ steps in 12 seeds. It reproduces a core of 15.6 ± 1.2 units by the paper's snapshot criterion, and 18.2 ± 1.1 by time-averaged outgoing weight above the mean, with 1.6 ± 2.6 periphery-to-core links (paper: 2). Five arms then ran for 10⁶ steps. With the whole core deleted, former periphery units formed a new core of 17.2 ± 0.8 units. The control that deletes as many periphery units formed one of 17.0 ± 1.1. The new core had 2.9 ± 4.8 periphery-to-core links. With a random half of the core deleted, 8.8 ± 0.8 periphery units joined the 8.5 survivors. With every weight given to the core cut to 10⁻³ of its value, the core's own members made up 92% of the core 10⁶ steps later. The differentiation recovers. Which units hold the core is set by the dynamics, not fixed by who held it first. One parameter point, one system size, 12 seeds. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CASE-340](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-340.md) | Many small closed groups of DeGroot averagers, each of size near the square root of log n, have a largest influence weight that vanishes while the chance that some group settles on a wrong consensus tends to one | The audit's sketch for [QUESTION-184](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-184.md), checked against Golub and Jackson's definitions ([LIT-999](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-999.md), reread 2026-11-22) and computed exactly. n agents in m = n/k closed groups of k = ⌈√(ln n)⌉, equal weights inside each group, independent Bernoulli(1/2) signals. Under Theorem 3 every influence weight is 1/k, which tends to 0; under Definition 3 the society is wise only if the largest deviation over all agents tends to 0 in probability. The chance that some group's consensus is exactly 0 or 1, missing the truth by 1/2, is 1 − (1 − 2^(1−k))^m, which tends to 1: 0.97 at n = 10, 0.9999 at n = 100, and 1 to six places from n = 10^4. A DeGroot iteration on a three-group matrix with transient members confirms Theorem 3's per-group normalization, and a Monte Carlo run agrees with the exact formula. With three groups, or with groups of size (ln n)², the same probability tends to 0. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [CASE-390](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-390.md) v2 | A simulated sensor network whose correspondences drift: revising them to reduce the sensors' disagreement restores consistency and not accuracy, revising them against beacons the world places through a channel the revision cannot rewrite or refuse restores accuracy, and a revisable beacon map or a right to refuse disagreeing beacons gives back part or all of the gain | The top rung [LEAD-177](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-177.md) asked for: a sensor network revising its correspondences, as [QUESTION-285](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-285.md)'s answer 3 proposes for Robinson's networks, whose correspondences are fixed. Four sensors report a moving target through maps that drift (a slow walk of every bias and, at step 500, a jump and a rotation of one sensor). The apparatus fuses by least squares and reports its consistency radius; 40 seeds, 3,000 steps. Fixed maps: late error 0.40, radius 1.16 (the radius flags the trouble). Revised by disagreement alone: radius 0.10, error 0.40, no better than fixed in 21 of 40 seeds. Revised only against beacons the world places, through a channel the revision cannot touch: error 0.044, as before the jump, in 40 of 40 seeds; sparser beacons give less (0.095 and 0.24). The beacon as one more revisable map: 0.30. Beacons admitted only when they agree with the current maps: 59 of 300 admitted, error 0.37; with a looser threshold, 260 admitted and error 0.045. The run makes [QUESTION-285](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-285.md)'s structural condition concrete in one construction. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
